title: Cluster Representation of Renormalization Group Transformations and a Rigorous Proof for Convergence of the RG-Flow of the Ising Model to Trivial Fixed Points away from Criticality
abstract: Many rigorous results in the modern era of statistical mechanics have been obtained through geometrical representations. A much studied tool in this setting is the random cluster representation of lattice spin models. Another area of statistical mechanics that is of great interest but lacking rigorous results is the theory of the renormalization group. This paper investigates the idea to find a common ground between these two concepts in order to obtain rigorous results on the renormalization group flow. A need for negative cluster-weights weakens the success of this approach. Nevertheless, we managed to establish a relation between the scaling limit of the renormalization group flow of the nearest-neighbour Ising model away from criticality with a simple one-dimensional dynamical system that follows the cluster connectivity of the renormalization group transformation. This allows for a rigorous proof of the convergence of this flow to the zero- and infinite-temperature fixed point respectively for a large family of renormalization group transformations. Explicit results will be established on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ followed by a discussion of the available generalizations to higher dimensions.
summary: This paper bridges the gap between the Random Cluster Model and the Renormalization Group theory to provide rigorous mathematical proofs for the RG flow of the Ising model away from its critical point. By mapping the RG flow onto a simple 1D dynamical system based on cluster connectivity, the authors prove convergence to high and low-temperature fixed points. This work advances the mathematical understanding of critical phenomena in statistical mechanics.
main_problem: To establish a rigorous mathematical foundation for the Renormalization Group (RG) flow, specifically by connecting RG transformations to geometrical representations like the random cluster model.
main_result: The paper rigorously proves the convergence of the RG flow for the nearest-neighbor Ising model away from criticality to the zero- and infinite-temperature fixed points for a large family of transformations.
method: The authors relate the scaling limit of the RG flow to a simple one-dimensional dynamical system governed by the cluster connectivity derived from the random cluster representation.
model_or_system: The primary system is the Ising model on the 2D square lattice ($\mathbb{Z}^2$), analyzed using the Random Cluster Model (RCM) framework. The analysis extends to higher-state Potts models.
key_observables: Convergence of the RG flow to trivial fixed points, correlation functions, and susceptibility ($\chi_p$).
important_parameters: Inverse temperature ($ eta$), the RCM parameter $p$, and the RG transformation parameters ($\alpha,  eta, \gamma$).
main_assumptions: The approach is weakened by the need for negative cluster-weights, and the results are explicitly established for the nearest-neighbor Ising model, with generalizations being an open question.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dynamics of the RG flow parameter $f$ for different parameter regimes and show possible block configurations for coarse-graining in the 3-states Potts model.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from introducing the need for rigorous RG foundations, detailing the RCM representation, analyzing the $2 	imes 2 	o 1$ RG transformation on the square lattice, and concluding with discussions on generalizations to higher dimensions and Potts models.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, the rigorous mathematical techniques involving dynamical systems and convergence proofs are highly relevant to understanding the dynamics of quantum many-body systems and quantum phase transitions.
